headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from LangGraph’s shared-state orchestration into Notion AI’s workspace-backed Q&A; no direct host-execution conflict, but cascading misuse remains plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can pass application-defined files/state through nodes and shared checkpointer state, while Notion AI ingests workspace pages for Q&A. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content in LangGraph outputs could be treated as instructions by Notion AI. The pair is not documented as isolated, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF LangGraph writes attacker-controlled text into shared graph state or files that Notion AI later reads
IF Notion AI treats workspace content as instruction-bearing rather than purely quoted material
mitigations: Prefix all LangGraph outputs with explicit data-only markers
Store untrusted LangGraph artifacts in a separate workspace/page
Add a manual review step before Notion AI consumes LangGraph-generated content
requires-engineering: enforce provenance tags across the handoff
requires-engineering: isolate the shared checkpointer from user-facing content

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph has broad network egress and can read/write application files, while Notion AI is vendor-hosted and sends workspace content to Notion backends and downstream model providers. If the pair shares workspace data, sensitive content can flow from LangGraph-managed state into Notion’s cloud processing. This is more than low because the default surfaces include shared content and external transmission.
conditions: IF LangGraph stores sensitive material in application-defined files or graph state
IF Notion AI is pointed at the same workspace pages or databases containing that material
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of shared pages and graph state
Use a separate Notion workspace for AI-assisted content
Redact secrets before LangGraph writes outputs
Restrict Notion AI access to non-sensitive pages
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction at the LangGraph-to-Notion boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph can write application-defined files and spawn subprocesses, but Notion AI cannot write the host filesystem or run local processes. Their write surfaces do not overlap at the OS level, so direct resource contention is limited. The remaining conflict is mostly on shared workspace content, which is narrower than the rubric’s medium/high overlap cases.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to edit the same application-defined files outside Notion
IF an orchestrator maps Notion outputs back into LangGraph-managed mutable state
mitigations: Separate mutable workspaces per agent
Avoid concurrent edits to the same artifact
Serialize handoffs through a single owner process
Use read-only exports from Notion into LangGraph
requires-engineering: add locking for shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph can generate intermediate facts or tool outputs, and Notion AI can summarize or rewrite workspace content. If Notion treats LangGraph output as authoritative, errors can cascade into polished but incorrect knowledge-base content. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF LangGraph-produced text is imported into Notion pages without human verification
IF Notion AI is asked to summarize or publish LangGraph outputs as facts
mitigations: Require human review before publishing
Mark LangGraph outputs as draft-only
Ask Notion AI to cite source pages explicitly
Compare outputs against original sources before acceptance
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking between agents

E_compliance.rationale: LangGraph is open-source and library-based, while Notion AI is closed-source, vendor-hosted, and processes workspace content through Notion backends and downstream model providers. If regulated or residency-sensitive data is placed into Notion pages, the compliance posture can differ materially from local LangGraph handling. The profiles do not prove a specific residency breach, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Notion workspace pages consumed by Notion AI
IF the organization requires local-only processing or a specific residency boundary
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Notion AI-enabled pages
Disable AI on sensitive workspaces
Use separate workspaces for regulated content
Review vendor retention settings before use
requires-engineering: route sensitive workflows to a compliant local system
